introduction.title: Grids
introduction.explanation: Every tile has a column and a row, counted from 0 like real code: the top left is column 0, row 0. Go to column and Go to row walk straight there.

realWords.text: Two numbers that name one tile are called coordinates. In code the column is x and the row is y, and both count from 0.
Curly brackets with named values inside make an object: several values kept together as one thing. { x: 4, y: 2 } is one place. A dot reads one part, so bird.x is its column.
An array of arrays is a 2D array: a list of rows, where each row is a list of tiles. Two indexes read one tile, row first: walls[y][x].
